tests.title: ArchiveDestination returns the free archive path and writes nothing
given: a root holding package 03_x and no archive/03_x
tests.when: afspec.ArchiveDestination(root/03_x, root) is called
then: it returns filepath.Join(root, "archive", "03_x") and a nil error
no directory named archive is created
the directory tree of root is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: p, err = ArchiveDestination(dir, root); assert err == nil; assert p == join(root,'archive','03_x'); assert !exists(join(root,'archive'))

tests.title: ArchiveDestination returns a *SaveError for a taken or unreadable destination
given: case A: root/archive/03_x already exists
case B: root/archive is a regular file, so the destination cannot be checked (ENOTDIR)
tests.when: ArchiveDestination(root/03_x, root) is called in each case
then: both return an empty path and an error for which errors.As(*SaveError) is true
in case A the message contains `archive conflict: <path> already exists`
nothing is written in either case
tests.pseudocode: p, err = ArchiveDestination(dir, root); assert p == ''; assert errors.As(err,&se); assert contains(se.Msg,'archive conflict: '+dest+' already exists')

tests.title: MoveUnderArchive moves an archived or superseded package without rewriting any file
given: a package copy at root/03_x with status archived, another with status superseded, no root/archive directory
a snapshot of every file's bytes and the modification times
tests.when: MoveUnderArchive(dir, root) is called for each package
then: it returns root/archive/03_x and a nil error
root/archive has mode 0755
the source directory no longer exists
every file at the destination is byte-identical to the snapshot, so status and updated_at are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: dest, err = MoveUnderArchive(dir, root); assert err==nil; assert !exists(dir); assert mode(root/archive)==0755; assert bytes(dest/*) == snapshot

tests.title: MoveUnderArchive returns the LoadError and moves nothing when the package does not load
given: a directory root/03_x whose requirements.json is malformed JSON
tests.when: MoveUnderArchive(dir, root) is called
then: it returns an empty path and an error for which errors.As(*LoadError) is true
root/03_x is unchanged and root/archive does not exist
tests.pseudocode: p, err = MoveUnderArchive(dir, root); assert p==''; assert errors.As(err,&le); assert exists(dir); assert !exists(root/archive)

tests.title: MoveUnderArchive refuses draft, active and sealed packages with a *LifecycleError
given: packages with status draft, active and sealed at root/NN_x
tests.when: MoveUnderArchive is called on each
then: each returns an empty path and a *LifecycleError
no archive directory is created and no directory is renamed
tests.pseudocode: for st in [draft,active,sealed]: p, err = MoveUnderArchive(pkg(st), root); assert errors.As(err,&lce); assert !exists(root/archive)

tests.title: MoveUnderArchive leaves the package in place when the destination is taken or the filesystem refuses
given: case A: archived package with root/archive/03_x existing
case B: archived package in a root made read-only (mode 0555), so creating archive/ fails (skipped when running as uid 0)
tests.when: MoveUnderArchive(dir, root) is called in each case
then: both return an empty path and a *SaveError
in case A the error is the one ArchiveDestination returns (archive conflict message)
the package is still at dir with byte-identical files
tests.pseudocode: p, err = MoveUnderArchive(dir, root); assert p==''; assert errors.As(err,&se); assert bytes(dir/*)==snapshot

tests.title: MoveToArchive transitions any non-archived package, a superseded one included, and moves it
given: a sealed package, a superseded package and an already-archived package, each at root/NN_x with a free destination
the existing TestMoveToArchive is kept unchanged
tests.when: MoveToArchive(dir, root) is called on each
then: each call returns nil
each package is at root/archive/NN_x with status archived
TestMoveToArchive passes unchanged
tests.pseudocode: assert MoveToArchive(dir,root)==nil; s=LoadSpec(root/archive/NN_x); assert s.Status=='archived'

tests.title: MoveToArchive with a taken destination returns a *SaveError and writes nothing
given: a sealed package at root/03_x and a directory root/archive/03_x
tests.when: MoveToArchive(dir, root) is called
then: it returns a *SaveError
the status at dir is still sealed
every file at dir is byte-identical to the snapshot taken before the call
tests.pseudocode: err = MoveToArchive(dir,root); assert errors.As(err,&se); assert LoadSpec(dir).Status=='sealed'; assert bytes(dir/*)==snapshot

tests.title: speca dispatches --status calls to the status form and honours --dry-run and --force
given: a spec root with a draft package that has an intent and validates, and a sealed package plus a replacing draft package
tests.when: Main is run with `<spec> --status active --dry-run`, `<spec> --status sealed`, and `<old> --status superseded --by <new>`
then: each call reaches the status form (the envelope carries changes, not a report)
the dry-run call has result.dry_run true and writes nothing
--force is accepted on the form without a usage error
tests.pseudocode: code = Main(['12_x','--status','active','--dry-run']); assert code==0; assert env.result.dry_run && len(env.result.changes)==1

tests.title: --status draft is a usage error that explains there is no way back to draft
given: a valid package directory
tests.when: Main is run with `<spec> --status draft`
then: exit code is 2, stage usage, category usage
the message says that no move leads back to draft and that a package whose intent must change is superseded by a new one
fix_hint is {flag: "--status", valid: ["active","sealed","superseded","archived"]}
no file is modified and there is no result
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','draft']); assert code==2; assert env.error.fix_hint == {flag:'--status',valid:[...four]}

tests.title: An unknown --status value is a usage error with the four valid targets
given: a valid package directory
tests.when: Main is run with `<spec> --status bogus`
then: exit code is 2, stage usage, category usage
fix_hint is {flag: "--status", valid: the four targets}
nothing is written
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','bogus']); assert code==2; assert env.error.fix_hint.valid==four

tests.title: Malformed flag combinations are usage errors that write nothing
given: a valid package directory and a replacing package
tests.when: Main is run with: `--status superseded` without --by; `--by <spec>` without --status; `--by` with `--status sealed`; `--status sealed --task 1 --state done`; `--status sealed --validate`; `--status sealed --list`; `--status sealed` with no positional input
then: every call exits 2 with stage usage and category usage
no envelope result is present
the file tree is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for args in cases: code=Main(args); assert code==2; assert env.error.stage=='usage'; assert env.result==nil

tests.title: A bad --by reference is a usage error, resolver failures prefixed with `--by:`
given: a sealed package 03_old and a replacing package 12_new
a second package whose spec_id equals 03_old's
tests.when: Main is run with `--by nonexistent`, `--by` naming the input's own directory, and `--by` naming the package with the same spec_id
then: each exits 2, stage usage, category usage
the resolver-failure message starts with `--by:`
nothing is written
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([old,'--status','superseded','--by','nope']); assert code==2; assert startsWith(env.error.message,'--by:')

tests.title: --schema and --help describe the --status form and match the golden file
given: cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json regenerated
tests.when: Main is run with --schema and with --help
then: the --schema output equals the golden file
the schema gives status as an enum of active, sealed, superseded, archived
help text and flag descriptions mention --status and --by
tests.pseudocode: out=Main(['--schema']); assert out==readFile(golden); assert schema.properties.status.enum==four

tests.title: Checks run in the specified order and the first refusal ends the call with no result
given: a draft package without an Intent section, with unknown keys, targeted at archived under a taken destination
a sealed package with an unknown key and a taken destination
tests.when: Main is run with --status for each, with and without --dry-run
then: the first package is refused by the move/target check, not by the unknown-key or destination checks
the sealed package is refused at the unknown-key check (stage status) before the destination check (stage archive)
the envelope has no result and the tree and modification times are unchanged, also under --dry-run
tests.pseudocode: for dry in [false,true]: code=Main(args+dry); assert env.error.stage==expected; assert env.result==nil; assert tree==snapshot

tests.title: Load failures and non-v2 packages are refused at stage load, also under --force
given: a malformed input package, a malformed --by package, and a package with schema_version 1
tests.when: Main is run with --status sealed --force on each
then: each exits 1, stage load, category input, and has no result
the message names the directory, and names --by when the replacing package is at fault
for the version-1 package the message says speca changes the state of format version 2 packages only
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed','--force']); assert code==1; assert env.error.stage=='load' && env.error.category=='input'

tests.title: A package already at the target status outside archive/ becomes a move-only call
given: an archived package and a superseded package at root/NN_x, neither under archive/
tests.when: Main is run with `--status archived` and `--status superseded --by <new>` respectively
then: neither call is refused as a disallowed transition
each exits 0 with changes containing a moved entry and no status entry
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','archived']); assert code==0; assert kinds(env.result.changes)==['moved']

tests.title: A disallowed transition is refused at stage status with the path and the allowed targets
given: an active package, a draft package, an archived package inside archive/, and a sealed package
tests.when: Main is run with: active --status archived; sealed --status sealed; archived(in archive/) --status active; draft --status sealed, all with --force
then: each exits 1, stage status, category lifecycle, and writes nothing
the message names the package, its status and the target
active → archived says to seal it first with `speca <spec> --status sealed`, then archive it
a same-status call says `already <status>`
fix_hint is {flag: --status, valid: allowed_status} when the allowed list is non-empty, and absent for the archived package
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([active,'--status','archived','--force']); assert code==1; assert contains(msg,'--status sealed'); assert fix_hint.valid==['sealed']

tests.title: The refusal names a shortest chain of ValidTransition steps, or none when none exists
given: the five statuses draft, active, sealed, superseded, archived
tests.when: for any ordered pair of distinct statuses (current, target) where ValidTransition(current, target) is false
then: when a chain of ValidTransition steps exists, the message names a chain whose length equals the breadth-first shortest length
when no chain exists, the message names no sequence of moves
tests.pseudocode: for (c,t) in pairs where !ValidTransition(c,t): msg=refusalMessage(c,t); sp=bfs(c,t); if sp!=nil: assert chainIn(msg)==sp-length else assert chainIn(msg)==none

tests.title: Sealing, archiving and superseding refuse a package with unknown keys without --force
given: an active package whose prd.md frontmatter has a key the schema does not allow, and a sealed package with an unknown key in tasks.json
tests.when: Main is run with --status sealed, and --status archived, without --force
then: each exits 1, stage status, category lifecycle
fix_hint.flag is --force
the message names each file and unknown key
no file is modified
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed']); assert code==1; assert env.error.fix_hint.flag=='--force'; assert contains(msg,'prd.md') && contains(msg,'badkey'); assert tree==snapshot

tests.title: --force proceeds past unknown keys with a high spec_invalid warning naming the keys
given: an active package with no open task whose prd.md has an unknown key
tests.when: Main is run with `--status sealed --force`
then: exit code is 0 and the package is sealed
the envelope has a warning with code spec_invalid and severity high naming the dropped key
the written package no longer contains the unknown key
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed','--force']); assert code==0; w=warning('spec_invalid'); assert w.severity=='high' && contains(w.message,'badkey')

tests.title: A taken archive destination is refused at stage archive before anything is written
given: a sealed package at root/03_x and a directory root/archive/03_x
tests.when: Main is run with `--status archived`, also with --force
then: exit code is 1, stage archive, category disk, resumable false
the message names the existing directory
there is no result and the package files are byte-identical, status still sealed
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','archived','--force']); assert code==1; assert env.error.stage=='archive'; assert env.resumable==false; assert env.result==nil; assert bytes(dir/*)==snapshot

tests.title: Activating a valid draft with an intent writes the status and intent hash
given: a draft package that validates and has a `## Intent` section
tests.when: Main is run with `<spec> --status active`
then: exit code is 0
result status is active and intent_hash is set
changes is [{kind: status, from: draft, to: active}]
the package is still in its original directory
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','active']); assert code==0; assert env.result.status=='active'; assert env.result.intent_hash!=''; assert env.result.changes==[{kind:'status',from:'draft',to:'active'}]

tests.title: Activation without an Intent section is refused even under --force
given: a draft package whose prd.md has no `## Intent` section
tests.when: Main is run with `--status active --force`
then: exit 1, stage status, category lifecycle
the message tells the caller to add `## Intent` to prd.md on a line of its own
no file is modified
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','active','--force']); assert code==1; assert contains(msg,'\n## Intent\n') ; assert tree==snapshot

tests.title: Activation of a package that does not validate is refused at stage validate
given: a draft package with an intent that fails Validate
tests.when: Main is run with `--status active` without --force
then: exit 1, stage validate, category invalid_spec
the message names the failing rules
fix_hint.flag is --force
no file is modified
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','active']); assert code==1; assert env.error.category=='invalid_spec'; assert env.error.fix_hint.flag=='--force'

tests.title: --force activates an invalid package with a high spec_invalid warning
given: a draft package with an intent that fails Validate
tests.when: Main is run with `--status active --force`
then: exit 0 and the package is active
a warning with code spec_invalid and severity high names the failing rules
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','active','--force']); assert code==0; assert warning('spec_invalid').severity=='high'

tests.title: Dry-run activation reports the hash ComputeIntentHash gives and leaves prd.md unchanged
given: a draft package that validates and has an intent
tests.when: Main is run with `--status active --dry-run`
then: result.intent_hash equals ComputeIntentHash(PRDBody)
prd.md bytes and modification time are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: h,_=ComputeIntentHash(body); Main([dir,'--status','active','--dry-run']); assert env.result.intent_hash==h; assert bytes(prd.md)==snapshot

tests.title: Sealing an active package with no drift and no open task writes the sealed status
given: an active package, all tasks done or dropped, intent unchanged
tests.when: Main is run with `--status sealed`
then: exit 0
result status is sealed
changes is [{kind: status, from: active, to: sealed}]
the package stays in its directory
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed']); assert code==0; assert env.result.status=='sealed'; assert env.result.changes==[{kind:'status',from:'active',to:'sealed'}]

tests.title: Sealing a package with intent drift is refused even under --force
given: an active package whose prd.md Intent section was edited after activation, and another whose Intent section was removed
tests.when: Main is run with `--status sealed --force`
then: exit 1, stage status, category lifecycle
the message says to restore the activated intent or write a new package that supersedes this one
there is no fix_hint
no file is modified
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed','--force']); assert code==1; assert env.error.fix_hint==nil; assert tree==snapshot

tests.title: Sealing with open tasks (optional ones included) is refused naming each task and state
given: an active package with one pending task and one optional in_progress task
tests.when: Main is run with `--status sealed` without --force
then: exit 1, stage status, category lifecycle
the message names each open task with its state and says to finish or drop it
fix_hint.flag is --force
no file is modified
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed']); assert contains(msg,'pending') && contains(msg,'in_progress'); assert env.error.fix_hint.flag=='--force'

tests.title: --force seals despite open tasks with a high tasks_open warning
given: an active package with a pending task and an in_progress task and no drift
tests.when: Main is run with `--status sealed --force`
then: exit 0, package sealed
a warning with code tasks_open and severity high lists each open task and its state
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed','--force']); assert code==0; w=warning('tasks_open'); assert w.severity=='high' && contains(w.message,'in_progress')

tests.title: Archiving a package outside archive/ writes the status then moves it
given: a sealed package at root/03_x; also a draft package at root/04_y and a superseded package at root/05_z
tests.when: Main is run with `--status archived` on each
then: exit 0 for each
the package is at root/archive/NN_x with status archived and the old directory is gone
changes are [status, moved] in that order
the moved change uses display paths
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','archived']); assert kinds(changes)==['status','moved']; assert LoadSpec(root/archive/03_x).Status=='archived'

tests.title: Archiving a package already under archive/ writes only the status
given: a sealed package at root/archive/03_x
tests.when: Main is run with `--status archived` on that path
then: exit 0
changes is [{kind: status}] only
the directory stays at root/archive/03_x
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([root+'/archive/03_x','--status','archived']); assert kinds(changes)==['status']; assert exists(root/archive/03_x)

tests.title: A move-only archive call rewrites no file and leaves updated_at alone
given: an archived package at root/03_x outside archive/, files snapshotted
tests.when: Main is run with `--status archived`
then: exit 0
changes is [{kind: moved}] only
files at root/archive/03_x are byte-identical, updated_at unchanged
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','archived']); assert kinds(changes)==['moved']; assert bytes(root/archive/03_x/*)==snapshot

tests.title: A replacing package that is superseded or archived is refused even under --force
given: a sealed old package and replacing packages with status superseded and archived
tests.when: Main is run with `--status superseded --by <replacing> --force`
then: exit 1, stage status, category lifecycle
fix_hint.flag is --by
no file is modified
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([old,'--status','superseded','--by',rep,'--force']); assert code==1; assert env.error.fix_hint.flag=='--by'; assert tree==snapshot

tests.title: Superseding writes banner and status, records supersedes, then moves the package
given: a sealed package 03_old and a draft replacing package 12_new with an empty supersedes
tests.when: Main is run with `03_old --status superseded --by 12_new`
then: exit 0
03_old sits at root/archive/03_old with status superseded and the DEPRECATED banner naming spec 12
12_new's supersedes ends with 03's spec_id
changes are [status, supersedes, moved] in that order
the supersedes change is {kind: supersedes, spec: <replacing id>, added: <old id>}
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([old,'--status','superseded','--by',new]); assert kinds(changes)==['status','supersedes','moved']; assert LoadSpec(new).Supersedes contains oldID

tests.title: A replacing package that cannot be saved yields a low supersedes_not_recorded warning and success
given: replacing packages that are: sealed; active with intent drift; carrying an unknown_field error; and a draft whose Save fails (directory made read-only)
tests.when: Main is run with `--status superseded --by <replacing> --force` for each
then: each exits 0 and the old package is superseded and under archive/
a warning code supersedes_not_recorded severity low names the replacing directory, the id not recorded and the reason
changes contain no supersedes entry
the replacing package's files are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: code=Main(args); assert code==0; w=warning('supersedes_not_recorded'); assert w.severity=='low'; assert kinds(changes)==['status','moved']

tests.title: A move-only supersede call skips Supersede, adds the missing id and moves
given: a superseded package at root/03_old outside archive/, and a replacing package whose supersedes lacks the old id
tests.when: Main is run with `03_old --status superseded --by <new>`
then: exit 0
changes are [supersedes, moved]
the old package's files are byte-identical at the new location
the replacing package's supersedes now contains the old id
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([old,'--status','superseded','--by',new]); assert kinds(changes)==['supersedes','moved']; assert bytes(root/archive/03_old/*)==snapshot

tests.title: The old spec_id appears exactly once in the replacing package's supersedes
given: a sealed old package and a draft replacing package with an arbitrary existing supersedes list
tests.when: for any sequence of one to five superseding calls naming the same old and replacing packages (including calls resuming after an interrupted move)
then: the old spec_id occurs exactly once in the replacing package's supersedes
entries that were already there keep their order
tests.pseudocode: for n in 1..5: repeat n times Main([oldPathNow,'--status','superseded','--by',new]); assert count(LoadSpec(new).Supersedes, oldID)==1

tests.title: Every written package gets updated_at set to the current UTC time in RFC 3339
given: a start time truncated to the second
an active package to seal, and a sealed one to supersede with a draft replacing package
tests.when: Main is run for sealing and for superseding
then: updated_at in each written prd.md (including the replacing package) parses with time.RFC3339 and is in UTC
it is not earlier than the start time truncated to the second
tests.pseudocode: t=parse(RFC3339, LoadSpec(dir).UpdatedAt); assert t.Location()==UTC; assert !t.Before(start.Truncate(second))

tests.title: A SaveError from the status write exits at stage write, category disk with the library message
given: an active package whose directory is read-only (mode 0555) so the temporary file cannot be created (skipped as uid 0)
tests.when: Main is run with `--status sealed`
then: exit 1, stage write, category disk
the message is the library's save error message
there is no result
tests.pseudocode: chmod(dir,0555); code=Main([dir,'--status','sealed']); assert code==1; assert env.error.stage=='write' && env.error.category=='disk'; assert env.result==nil

tests.title: A LifecycleError or IntentError that reaches the write is reported at stage status, category lifecycle
given: the status form with a stubbed library call that returns *LifecycleError, then *IntentError
tests.when: the write step runs
then: each exit is 1, stage status, category lifecycle
tests.pseudocode: for e in [&LifecycleError{}, &IntentError{}]: stub.transition=e; code=run(); assert code==1; assert stage=='status' && category=='lifecycle'

tests.title: A move failure after the status write exits at stage archive, resumable, with result and next
given: a sealed package at root/03_x in a read-only root (mode 0555 on root, package directory writable) so the status write succeeds and the rename fails; skipped as uid 0
the same case for superseding with --by
tests.when: Main is run with `--status archived`, and with `--status superseded --by <new>`
then: exit 1, stage archive, category disk, resumable true, retryable false
the message names the directory the package is in now and its new status and says that running the same call again moves it
the summary says the status was written and the move was not
result is present with spec_dir at the current location, the new status, and changes listing what was written
next holds the same call against the current spec_dir, with --by when superseding
tests.pseudocode: code=Main([dir,'--status','archived']); assert code==1; assert env.resumable && !env.retryable; assert env.result.changes==[status]; assert env.next[0].flags==['--status','archived']

tests.title: Re-running the same call after an archive-stage failure only moves the package
given: a package left after a failed archive call, with its files snapshotted, and the cause (read-only root) cleared
tests.when: the same call is run again
then: exit 0
changes contain only moved (and supersedes if it was still missing)
the files at the new location are byte-identical to the snapshot taken after the failed call
tests.pseudocode: fail=Main(args); chmod(root,0755); snap=snapshot(dir); code=Main(args); assert code==0; assert kinds(changes)==['moved']; assert bytes(dest/*)==snap

tests.title: A read-back failure after a successful write exits at stage load and keeps the changes
given: the status form with a stubbed read-back loader that fails after Transition succeeded
tests.when: the call runs with `--status sealed`
then: exit 1, stage load, category input
the result is present and carries changes [{kind: status, from: active, to: sealed}]
tests.pseudocode: stub.loadAfterWrite=fail; code=run(); assert env.error.stage=='load'; assert len(env.result.changes)==1

tests.title: Result.Resumable is true only for the archive-stage failure
given: Result values for: success, refusal, write-stage failure, load-stage failure after write, archive-stage failure after a status write
tests.when: Resumable() is called on each, and each is passed through Run.Envelope
then: only the archive-stage failure returns true and has envelope resumable true
all others return false
tests.pseudocode: assert Result{archiveFail}.Resumable()==true; for r in others: assert !r.Resumable()

tests.title: The success result is read back from where the package now is, in report-form shape
given: a sealed package at root/03_x
tests.when: Main is run with `--status archived`
then: result.spec_dir is the display path of root/archive/03_x
the result has the report-form fields (status, tasks, allowed_status, valid and so on) from a fresh LoadSpec
changes are ordered status, supersedes, moved with the specified shapes
tests.pseudocode: Main([dir,'--status','archived']); assert result.spec_dir==display(root/archive/03_x); assert result.status=='archived'

tests.title: --dry-run gives the same exit, refusals, warnings, changes and result and writes nothing
given: a set of calls: activation, sealing with --force and open tasks, archiving, superseding with a replacing package, a refusal, each with a snapshot of tree and modification times
tests.when: each is run with --dry-run and then without
then: exit codes, error stage/category, warnings and changes match between the two runs
result.dry_run is true only in the dry-run run
the tree and every modification time are unchanged after the dry run
tests.pseudocode: d=Main(args+['--dry-run']); assert tree==snapshot; r=Main(args); assert d.changes==r.changes && d.exit==r.exit; assert d.result.dry_run

tests.title: The summary sentence has the specified form for each move and under --dry-run
given: successful calls for activate, seal, archive, supersede and move-only
tests.when: each call is run, with and without --dry-run
then: summaries equal `speca: activated <name>`, `speca: sealed <name>`, `speca: archived <name>, moved to <display path>`, `speca: superseded <name> by <spec_id>, moved to <display path>`, `speca: moved <name> to <display path>`
under --dry-run each ends with ` (dry run; nothing written)`
tests.pseudocode: assert env.summary=='speca: sealed 09_x'; assert dry.summary==env.summary+' (dry run; nothing written)'

tests.title: After a call, next is the task claim after activation and empty otherwise
given: a draft package whose next_task is ready; sealed, archived, superseded and move-only calls; a refusal
tests.when: each call is run without --dry-run
then: after activation next is [`speca <spec_dir> --task N --state in_progress`] for next_task
after sealing, archiving, superseding, move-only calls and refusals next is empty
